unin.title: Remove programs
unin.lead: The same list as in Control Panel. Preinstalled manufacturer software and expired antivirus trials can be removed here in one go — on request completely, including leftover folders and registry keys.

unin.confirmMessage: {anzahl} program(s) will be removed. This cannot be undone — they have to be installed again afterwards.
unin.confirmLoud: {anzahl} of them bring their own wizard and will ask again themselves. WinZii has to wait for that — please click those windows through.
unin.leftoverMessage: {entfernt} removed, {fehlgeschlagen} failed. The uninstallers left things behind ({groesse}). Registry keys are exported to a .reg file before they go. Deleted folders are gone for good — including any settings and profiles inside them.

unin.msgNoCommand: no usable uninstall command on record

unin.detailOutside: not removed — outside the permitted areas
unin.logOutside: Leftover skipped, outside the permitted areas: {pfad}
unin.undoHint: Folders are deleted for good; removed registry keys sit in the backup folder as a .reg file.

auto.title: What starts when you sign in
auto.lead: Every entry here lengthens startup and uses memory. Disabled entries are kept and can be switched back on at any time — nothing is deleted.
auto.listHint: Click to switch on or off
auto.noticeDisable: When in doubt disable rather than delete: the entry stays and can be brought back with one click. Programs like antivirus or cloud storage should stay on.

clean.title: Free up disk space
clean.lead: Analyse first, then choose deliberately. WinZii only ever deletes caches and system leftovers — never your own files.
clean.resultHint: Click “Analyse” to find out how much space is in use.
clean.noticeBrowsers: Browsers should be closed before deleting, otherwise locked files stay behind. Sign-ins, bookmarks and passwords are not affected.
clean.totalHint: deletable in total — the selection decides what actually goes
clean.nothingMessage: The chosen entries are for analysis only. WinZii deletes nothing there.
clean.confirmRisky: Among them are entries that cannot be undone.
clean.confirmDryRun: Dry run: this only lists what would be deleted. {rest}
clean.lineDryRun: Dry run finished — nothing was deleted.
clean.lineLocked: {anzahl} item(s) were locked and stayed behind — with caches that is normal.
clean.filesMixed: {gesamt} file(s), {alt} of them older than 90 days ({groesse})
clean.detailDismOnly: size only known once DISM has analysed it
clean.logAnalysisOnly: analysis only — nothing is deleted here
clean.logDismRunning: DISM is running — this takes a few minutes...
clean.logDismFailed: DISM ended with code {code} — details in %windir%\Logs\DISM\dism.log

diag.title: Fault analysis
diag.lead: Event logs, blue screens and drive health — summarised and put into plain language instead of raw data.
diag.reliabilityHint: Crashes, application faults and installations on one timeline. This is where you see whether a problem coincides with an installation — the event list does not show that.
diag.noticeReadOnly: The analysis only reads and changes nothing. The repair tools below do reach into the system.
diag.relNone: No entries — reliability monitoring is empty on this PC
diag.relClean: {anzahl} entries, no crashes or application errors among them
diag.relMore: {anzahl} older entries are in the report

diag.eventsMore: {anzahl} further entries are in the report
diag.bootAverage: On average {dauer} until the desktop is ready
diag.dumpsNone: No bluescreens in the last 90 days
diag.reportMessage: The report is on the WinZii drive and opens in any browser — also suitable as a printout for the customer.
diag.sfcMessage: Windows compares every system file against the original and replaces damaged ones. Takes 5 to 15 minutes.
diag.dismMessage: DISM checks the Windows image and downloads missing parts from Microsoft if needed. Takes 5 to 20 minutes and needs internet.
diag.chkdskMessage: Checks the file system while Windows runs. No restart is needed for this.
diag.noBatteryMessage: This PC has no battery — so a report is not possible.
diag.hintNoRights: The performance log could not be opened — administrator rights are missing for that.
diag.hintNoBoots: No boots have been recorded yet. The value is available after the next restart.

diag.hintNoBootsShort: No boots have been recorded yet.

diag.bootVerySlow: Startup takes far too long. Thin out the startup items and check the disk condition — with old hard disks that is the most common reason.
diag.dumpUnknownCause: The stop code is not in the translation table.
diag.dumpUnknownRec: Analyse the dump with WinDbg, or look the code up.
diag.noteWear: wear above 80 percent — plan a replacement

diag.logDismRunning: Checking the Windows image ({aktion}) — this takes 5 to 20 minutes...

diag.dismOther: DISM ended with code {code}. Details in %windir%\Logs\DISM\dism.log.
diag.chkdskNeedsReboot: Cleanup needed — schedule a check with a restart.

drv.title: Drivers
drv.lead: Devices that are not working — and the driver backup, without which a laptop can easily end up with no Wi-Fi after a fresh install.
drv.devicesHint: Reads Device Manager and puts the error codes into plain language.
drv.tipShowMicrosoft: Microsoft's own drivers are almost always old and perfectly fine all the same.
drv.inventoryHint: Oldest first. With blue screens and crashes the suspect is usually right at the top.
drv.backupTitle: Back up drivers to the drive
drv.backupHint: The backup goes next to WinZii under offline\treiber and can be restored in one go after a fresh install.
drv.noticeBackup: A driver backup before a reinstall saves you hunting for downloads that often no longer exist for older notebooks.
drv.onlyUnplugged: Only unplugged devices — nothing to do
drv.logDevicesWithError: {anzahl} device(s) with an error code found.
drv.driversFromVendors: {anzahl} of {gesamt} drivers come from device manufacturers
drv.driversHidden: {anzahl} newer drivers are not listed here
drv.driverListFailed: The driver list could not be queried.
drv.thirdPartyUnknown: cannot be determined — administrator rights are missing
drv.hintNoRoomAtAll: There is not even room for the small backup.
drv.hintRoomForSmall: There is not room for all drivers — the small backup fits.
drv.noBackupYet: There is no backup on this drive yet
drv.exportMessage: The drivers are written to offline\treiber\{computer}. Depending on volume that takes a few minutes.
drv.exportMessage2: The recommended selection leaves out what Windows brings along itself — only those are not restored by a reinstall.
drv.exportFailed: Nothing was backed up. The driver export needs administrator rights.
drv.actionExport: {anzahl} driver package(s) backed up to the drive ({groesse})
drv.importMessage: The drivers from the chosen backup are added to Windows and installed for matching devices. Windows does not replace existing, newer drivers. A restart after importing is sensible.
drv.importWarnOther: Careful: the drive also holds backups from other machines (this PC is called {computer}). Only import another device's drivers if it really is the same hardware.
drv.err1Text: The device is not configured correctly.
drv.err3Text: The driver is damaged, or memory is short.
drv.err3Fix: Reinstall the driver, then check the memory.
drv.err10Fix: Usually a wrong or outdated driver. Install a newer driver from the manufacturer.
drv.err12Text: There are not enough free resources.
drv.err12Fix: Remove another expansion card, or free resources in the BIOS.
drv.err14Text: The device only works properly after a restart.
drv.err18Text: The drivers have to be reinstalled.
drv.err18Fix: Remove the driver and install it again.
drv.err19Text: The configuration in the registry is damaged.
drv.err19Fix: Uninstall the device and let it be detected again.
drv.err28Text: No driver is installed for this device.
drv.err31Text: Windows cannot load the required drivers.
drv.err37Text: The driver could not be started.
drv.err39Text: The driver is missing or damaged.
drv.err43Text: Windows stopped the device because of a reported error.
drv.err45Text: The device is not connected at the moment.
drv.err45Fix: Just a note about a previously used device — not an error.
drv.err52Text: The driver's signature cannot be verified.
drv.err52Fix: Unsigned driver. Only fetch it from the manufacturer.
drv.fixGeneric: Look in Device Manager and renew the driver.
drv.logExportTest: [Test] drivers would be backed up to {ziel}
drv.logExportRunning: Backing up drivers — depending on volume this takes a few minutes...
drv.importedCount: {anzahl} driver package(s) imported. A restart is recommended.
drv.importedNone: The operation ran through. Apparently there were no new drivers.
drv.err28Fix: The classic after a reinstall — install the driver from the manufacturer or from the backup.
drv.err43Fix: Often a hardware defect or a faulty driver version. With USB devices, try a different port first.

off.lead: Microsoft Office through the official deployment tool — or LibreOffice if there is no licence.

off.libreLead: Free of charge and without a licence key. Also opens and saves the Microsoft Office formats — perfectly sufficient for most private customers.

off.stateNone: No Office is installed on this PC

off.dryRunInstall: Nothing was changed. The log says what would have happened.

opt.confirmDryRun: Dry run: this only logs what would happen. {rest}
opt.optionRestorePoint: Create a system restore point first (recommended)
opt.optionProtectionOff: — system protection is off and stays on afterwards
opt.lineFailed: {anzahl} with errors — details in the log.
opt.lineReboot: A restart is needed for everything to take effect.

log.title: Session log

log.outputHint: Reports are stored on the WinZii drive.
log.handoverHint: Sums up in the customer's language what was done, how much space was gained, how the PC is equipped and what is still open. The log above is a developer log and unsuitable for that.

log.logSaveFailed: The log could not be saved: {grund}

log.readOnlyDrive: The drive is write-protected — nothing can be saved.

rest.title: Restore
rest.lead: The other half of the data move: whatever was backed up on the data page comes back onto the PC here — Wi-Fi networks, bookmarks, printers and network drives.
rest.sourceHint: The search covers offline\daten. A backup from a different machine can be restored as well — it is then marked as such.
rest.wlanHint: The profiles are created for all users. If the backup was made without keys, the entry is created but the PC will not connect on its own.
rest.bookmarksHint: The existing bookmark file is replaced. WinZii puts a copy ending in .winzii-vorher next to it first. The browser has to be closed.
rest.devicesHint: A printer can only be created if its driver is already installed — otherwise it appears here as a note rather than an error. Protected shares ask for their own credentials.
rest.noticeWrites: Every button asks first and says exactly what it creates. Restoring changes this PC — unlike the data page, which only reads.
rest.hintBackupFirst: Back up on the “Data” page first, then there is something here to restore.
rest.hintTopSource: The topmost backup is used. Use the button below to switch.
rest.sourceMessage: Which backup should be restored from? A backup from another machine does not necessarily fit: printers hang on different ports there, and browser profiles have different names.
rest.noWlanInBackup: No Wi-Fi networks in the backup
rest.withoutKey: without key — will not connect by itself
rest.wlanSomeWithoutKey: {anzahl} Wi-Fi network(s), {ohne} of them without a key
rest.noDevicesInBackup: No device list in the backup
rest.hintDeviceList: The device list is created on the “Data” page via “Back up printers and drives”.
rest.foreignWarning: Careful: the backup comes from {rechner}, not from this PC.
rest.wlanMessage: These networks are created for all users of this PC. An existing profile of the same name is overwritten.
rest.extraWithoutKey: created, but without a key — the password has to be entered again here
rest.marksMessage: The existing bookmarks of these profiles are replaced. WinZii puts a copy of the previous file alongside, with the extension .winzii-vorher.
rest.marksRunning: {browser} is running — while the browser is open it writes the old bookmarks back when it closes. Please close it first.
rest.extraBlocked: skipped, because the browser was still running
rest.printersMessage: These printers are set up anew. Existing ones stay untouched. If the driver is not set up yet, WinZii takes it from the Windows driver store — nothing is downloaded.
rest.printersMessage2: A USB port like USB001 cannot be created by hand — it only appears once the printer is plugged in. Such entries are skipped and named afterwards. Network printers via an IP address are created in full by WinZii.
rest.extraMissingDriver: skipped, because the driver could not be set up
rest.extraMissingPort: skipped, because the port does not exist here — it only appears with the device attached
rest.drivesMessage: These connections are created permanently. A drive letter already in use is skipped. If a share needs a sign-in, Windows asks for it itself — WinZii stores no passwords.
rest.dryRunMessage: Dry run: nothing was changed. The lines in the log show what would have happened.
rest.nothingToDo: There was nothing to do — everything was already set up.

rest.logDriverInstalled: Driver “{name}” set up from the driver store
rest.logPortLeftOver: Port {name} was left over — please remove it in the printer settings.
rest.logDriveTaken: Drive {buchstabe}: is already in use — skipped

tool.title: Repair
tool.lead: The moves needed most often day to day — each with an explanation of what actually happens.
tool.checkHint: Checks network adapter, IP address, router, name resolution and internet access one after another — and says which of the buttons below helps.
tool.netHint: Try the quick refresh first. The full reset helps when nothing works at all, and needs a restart.
tool.updateHint: Resets the update cache. The old folders are only renamed, not deleted — Windows recreates them at the next update.
tool.printerHint: For when print jobs are stuck in the queue and cannot be deleted.
tool.defenderHint: A quick scan by Windows Defender. With “the PC is slow”, malware is among the most common causes.
tool.restoreHint: Worth doing before bigger changes. Windows normally allows only one point per day — WinZii lifts that limit briefly.
tool.bloatHint: Apps that come with Windows and only take up space on most customer machines.
tool.noticeAsksFirst: Every action here asks first and records what it does. In dry run it is only logged.
tool.scanMessage: Windows Defender checks the usual hiding places for malware. Depending on the PC this takes five to fifteen minutes; WinZii cannot be used in the meantime.
tool.renewMessage: {anzahl} step(s) carried out. Check whether the connection works now — otherwise the full reset helps.
tool.resetMessage: Winsock and the IP stack are reset to factory settings, the DNS cache is cleared and the proxy removed. A restart is needed afterwards. VPN programs may have to set up their drivers again.
tool.actionReset: Network settings reset to factory state
tool.resetDoneMessage: {anzahl} step(s) done. The PC has to restart for the changes to take effect.
tool.dnsQuad9: 9.9.9.9 — blocks known malicious sites, operated in Switzerland
tool.dnsRouter: The settings come from the router again
tool.dnsMessage: The change applies to every active network adapter. The previous settings are saved under backups\ first — on a PC with a fixed server (company network, own router) that is the only way back, because “back to router” only means: obtain automatically again.
tool.dnsBackupHint: The previous settings are available as a file.
tool.wuMessage: The update services are stopped, the SoftwareDistribution and catroot2 folders renamed and the services started again. Windows re-creates both folders at the next update. Updates already downloaded are fetched again.
tool.wuOk: The cache was reset. Now search for updates again in Settings.
tool.wuFail: Nothing could be renamed — the folders were locked. Try again after a restart.
tool.spoolerMessage: All waiting print jobs are discarded and the print service is restarted. Installed printers are kept.
tool.rpMessage: Windows creates a system restore point. That takes up to a minute and needs some disk space. If system protection for C: is off, it is switched on for this and stays on.
tool.rpFail: The point could not be created. Most common cause: system protection is off for drive C:.
tool.bloatNone: Nothing found — this PC is already tidy
tool.logBloatFound: {anzahl} preinstalled app(s) found that can be removed.
tool.bloatMessage: {anzahl} app(s) will be removed for all users and no longer provisioned for newly created accounts either. They can be reinstalled from the Microsoft Store if needed.
tool.bloatRecordHint: What was removed is in the list below.
tool.dnsBackupHeader: DNS configuration before WinZii changed it
tool.logDnsUnreadable: DNS configuration could not be read: {grund}
tool.logDnsBackupTest: [Test] DNS configuration would be backed up
tool.logDnsBackupFailed: DNS backup could not be written: {grund}
tool.logWuTest: [Test] the Windows Update cache would be reset
tool.msgFoldersRecreated: Windows re-creates the folders at the next update. The old folders can be deleted after a few days.
tool.logSpoolerDone: {anzahl} stuck print job(s) removed, service restarted
tool.recordRestore: To get them back: search the Microsoft Store and install again.
tool.logRecordFailed: List of removed apps could not be written: {grund}
tool.verdictNoAdapter: No network connection is active at all — neither cable nor Wi-Fi.
tool.recNoAdapter: Check the network cable, or switch Wi-Fi on. If Device Manager shows a network adapter with an error mark, the driver is missing — the “Drivers” page helps then.
tool.verdictNoIp: The network adapter is connected, but received no IP address.
tool.recNoIp: Try “Refresh IP address” first. If nothing changes, the router hands out no addresses (DHCP), or a fixed address is entered incorrectly.
tool.verdictApipa: The PC gave itself the address {adresse} — it received none from the router.
tool.recApipa: This is nearly always the router or the cable: try “Refresh IP address”, otherwise restart the router. On Wi-Fi, check whether the right network is connected at all.
tool.verdictNoGateway: No default gateway is configured — the PC does not know where to send requests to the internet.
tool.recNoGateway: Usually a wrongly set fixed IP configuration. “Refresh IP address” restores DHCP.
tool.verdictRouterAndDns: The router at {adresse} does not answer, and name resolution fails too.
tool.recRouterAndDns: Restart the router and check the cable. On Wi-Fi, poor reception can be the cause too.
tool.verdictDnsOnly: The router answers, but internet addresses cannot be translated into IP addresses — that is a pure DNS problem.
tool.recDnsOnly: Switch to “Cloudflare” or “Quad9” below. That fixes it nearly always and can be reverted to “back to router” at any time.
tool.verdictOk: The network is fine — name resolution and internet access both answer.
tool.verdictOkAll: The network is fine — router, name resolution and internet access all answer.
tool.verdictOkNoPing: The router at {adresse} does not answer ping requests — some devices block that on principle, and nothing is broken because of it.
tool.recOk: If the customer still complains about “no internet”, it comes down to a single program: an antivirus with its own firewall, VPN software, or a proxy in the browser.
tool.verdictPortal: A sign-in portal sits in the way — typical of hotel, guest or company Wi-Fi.
tool.recPortal: Open any page in the browser; the sign-in page then appears by itself.
tool.verdictCertificate: The connection works, but the security certificate is rejected. {zeithinweis}
tool.recCertificate: Two usual causes: the system clock is wrong (then no certificate checks out), or an intercepting antivirus or company proxy sits in between. A network reset does not help here.
tool.verdictNoInternet: Router and name resolution work, but no connection to the outside is established.
tool.recNoInternet: Usually a firewall or antivirus blocks it. If parental controls or a time limit are set on the router, those apply here too.
tool.clockBeforeInstall: Careful: the system clock reads {datum}, which is before Windows was installed — it is wrong.
tool.clockWrong: Careful: the system clock reads {datum} and is plainly wrong.
tool.clockPlausible: The system clock reads {datum} and looks plausible.
tool.logScanTest: [Test] a quick virus scan would be started
tool.logScanRunning: Quick virus scan running — this takes a few minutes...
tool.scanFound: {anzahl} detection(s). Defender moved them to quarantine.
tool.scanFailed: The scan could not be started: {grund}

data.title: Data
data.lead: The question before every fresh install: what needs backing up? This page lists where the data lives — and warns about the places where a backup likes to quietly miss.
data.scanHint: Only reading and measuring happens here. WinZii deliberately does not copy the actual data — that belongs to a backup program, not to a tool like this one.
data.profilesHint: Size of the personal folders per account. The total is the space a full backup needs.
data.moveHint: Copies the personal folders of an account to another drive — to an external disk, not to the technician's stick. The source is left untouched: WinZii copies and deletes nothing.
data.outlookHint: PST files hold folders that exist only on this PC. OST files are merely a copy of the mailbox and are rebuilt.
data.browserHint: Saved passwords stay encrypted and cannot be taken along — the bookmarks can.
data.devicesHint: So that nothing is forgotten after a fresh install. The list is saved as geraete.json and can be recreated on the “Restore” page.
data.keysHint: These exports write passwords and keys in plain text onto the drive. That is why each one asks separately.
data.reportHint: Sums the inventory up as a printable page — the checklist for the fresh install.
data.noticeReadOnly: The survey only reads. The buttons below write — exports to the drive, the file move to a second drive, the OneDrive download to the system disk. Each one asks first and says exactly what will happen. Nothing is ever deleted.
data.noAccessProfile: no access — the profile belongs to another account
data.oneDriveNotSetUp: OneDrive is not set up on this PC
data.oneDriveNoAccount: No account signed in — there are no files in the cloud that could go missing when copying.
data.oneDriveCloudOnly: {anzahl} file(s) exist only in the cloud
data.oneDriveAllLocal: All files are on the disk as well
data.logPlaceholders: OneDrive: {anzahl} file(s) are only placeholders — download them before copying.
data.noAccessHint: Without access to the personal folders nothing can be copied. Start with administrator rights and other accounts become readable too.
data.noteWinZiiHere: WinZii runs from here — not suitable for customer data
data.noteTooSmall: not enough room for the largest account
data.noTargetHint: Nothing is connected apart from the system drive. A backup onto the same disk does not survive a reinstall — please plug in an external disk.
data.outlookNone: Outlook is not set up, or works only on the web.
data.browsersNone: Neither Edge, Chrome, Brave nor Firefox has created a profile here.
data.bookmarkMessage: The bookmark files are copied to the drive. Passwords are not included — they stay encrypted in the profile.
data.actionBookmarks: Bookmarks from {anzahl} browser profile(s) backed up
data.hydrateMessage: OneDrive will be told to keep all files permanently on this PC. Only then does a backup copy real files instead of empty placeholders — there are {anzahl} of them here.
data.hydrateMessage2: That needs room on the system disk and takes a while depending on volume and connection. WinZii waits at most 15 minutes and then says honestly whether it finished.
data.hydrateNotRunning: OneDrive is not running. Without the service nothing happens — please start it and sign in first.
data.hydrateDoneAll: All files are on the disk now. A backup will capture them completely.
data.hydrateDonePartial: Not finished yet. Only copy once no placeholders are left — otherwise empty shells end up in the backup.
data.chooseAccountMessage: Which account's personal folders should be copied?
data.chooseTargetMessage: {konto} uses {groesse}. Where should the copy go?
data.chooseTargetHint: An external disk is the right choice. The technician's stick is not: it holds up to four gigabytes of Office cache, and customer data does not belong on a tool that goes into the next PC.
data.warnNotEnoughRoom: Only {frei} free on {laufwerk} — that is not enough for {noetig}.
data.warnFat32Target: The target is FAT32: files over 4 GB fail individually, the rest is copied anyway.
data.warnWinZiiTarget: The target is the WinZii drive. Customer data has no business being there.
data.copyMessage: The folders are copied to {ziel}. The source stays fully intact — WinZii deletes and moves nothing.
data.copyPartial: Part of it did not work. The reasons are in the log. The source is unchanged.
data.copyDone: {groesse} copied. Please spot-check the target before anything is deleted on the source PC.
data.deviceMessage: Printers and network drives are written to the drive as geraete.json. The “Restore” page can re-create them after a reinstall. Passwords for protected shares are not included.
data.actionDevices: Printers and network drives backed up ({anzahl} entry/entries)
data.wlanMessage: {anzahl} saved network(s) will be written to the drive as files.
data.wlanMessage2: With keys, the Wi-Fi passwords sit in these files in plain text. That is the whole point — without them the PC cannot get online after a reinstall. Do not hand the drive to strangers afterwards.
data.wlanNoteKeys: The files contain the passwords in plain text.
data.bitlockerMessage: The recovery keys for {laufwerke} will be written to a text file in the backup folder.
data.bitlockerMessage2: This key opens the drive. It belongs somewhere safe — but without it the drive is locked for good after a mainboard swap or BIOS update.
data.bitlockerNoKeys: No key could be read. That needs administrator rights.
data.bitlockerSaved: {anzahl} key(s) backed up. Please treat the file as confidential.
data.bitlockerDryRun: {anzahl} key(s) found — nothing was written in dry run.
data.reportDoneMessage: The handover report is in the reports folder. Open it in a browser and choose “Print” there.
data.logOneDriveAborted: OneDrive folder very large — counting stopped after 45 s ({anzahl} file(s) checked).
data.warnIncompleteCount: The OneDrive folder is so large that the check was stopped — the numbers are incomplete. Before copying, choose “Always keep on this device” in OneDrive and wait for the download.
data.warnPlaceholders: Careful: {anzahl} file(s) exist only in the cloud, not on this disk. Copying the OneDrive folder as it is backs up empty placeholders. Choose “Always keep on this device” in OneDrive first and wait for the download.
data.outlookPst: PST — holds its own data, must be backed up
data.outlookOst: OST — cache only, will be rebuilt
data.logWlanTest: [Test] Wi-Fi networks would be backed up to {ziel}
data.logWlanWithKeys: including keys — please treat as confidential
data.logBitlockerTest: [Test] BitLocker keys would be backed up
data.fileBitlockerNote1: These keys open the encrypted drives of this PC.
data.fileBitlockerNote2: Please keep them safe and do not leave them lying around.
data.logDevicesTest: [Test] {drucker} printer(s) and {laufwerke} network drive(s) would be written to {ziel}
data.logDevicesUnsavable: Device list could not be saved: {grund}
data.logDevicesSaved: {drucker} printer(s) and {laufwerke} network drive(s) backed up to {ziel}
data.logBookmarkFailed: Bookmarks from {browser} could not be copied: {grund}
data.logCopyCancelled: File move cancelled — folders already copied are kept.
data.reasonNotRunning: OneDrive is not running. Without the service nothing downloads — please start OneDrive and sign in.
data.logHydrateTest: [Test] {pfad} would be set to “Always keep on this device”
data.reasonAlreadyLocal: All files were already on the disk.
data.reasonAttribFailed: The attribute could not be set (exit code {code}).
data.reasonCancelled: Cancelled. OneDrive keeps downloading in the background — the attribute stays set.
data.reasonStalled: Nothing has arrived for a minute. Please check in OneDrive whether syncing is paused.
data.logHydrateDone: OneDrive: all files are now local.
data.reasonTimeout: The time budget of {minuten} minutes ran out. OneDrive keeps downloading in the background.
